treatment_description: Tibetan barley-wheat rotation, ≥10 years (CW10+)
control_description: Continuous Tibetan barley cropping, ≥10 years (CC10+)
notes: SD values estimated from error bars in Figure 1. Text states CW10+ yield was 17% higher than CC10+; calculated effect from means is 16.8%. This is the strongest rotation benefit, observed in long-term fields. No CR10+ treatment exists in the study. CC10+ has notably higher SD (wider spread) reflecting greater yield variability in long-term continuous cropping. IMPORTANT: Neither wheat nor rape are legumes. This paper studies non-legume rotations (wheat=Poaceae, rape=Brassica) on the Tibetan Plateau. It may have limited relevance for a legume rotation meta-analysis, though it documents rotation benefits for the subsequent barley crop.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT: This paper shows NEGATIVE legume rotation effect because the field is heavily infested with P. thornei root-lesion nematode. Legumes (soybean, mungbean, black gram) are susceptible hosts that multiply nematode populations, whereas non-legume crops (especially millets, panicum, sorghum) are partially resistant and suppress nematodes. The typical N-fixation benefit of legumes is overwhelmed by the nematode damage pathway. From regression analysis, yield loss was 62% at maximum nematode density (8099 P. thornei/kg soil at 0-90cm).
